---
title: "Choosing a palette style"
description: "Qualitative, diverging and sequential palettes, and when to use each."
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.2, dpi = 120, message = FALSE)
library(PortinariColors)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
```

Like RColorBrewer and MetBrewer, PortinariColors groups its palettes by the
kind of data they suit.

```{r}
portinari.palettes()[, c("palette", "category", "n_colors", "cvd_n")]
```

## Qualitative: unordered groups

Distinct hues with no implied order. Asking for `n` colors returns the `n`
most distinct ones.

```{r, fig.height = 1.6}
show_portinari(category = "qualitative")
```

```{r}
ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_portinari("cafe", name = "Drive")
```

## Sequential: ordered values

Colors run from dark to light. Discrete subsets keep both ends and space the
rest evenly.

```{r, fig.height = 1.6}
show_portinari(category = "sequential")
```

```{r}
ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_portinari("guerra_azul", type = "continuous", direction = -1) +
  coord_cartesian(expand = FALSE)
```

## Diverging: values around a midpoint

Two dark arms meet in a light center, so the middle of the scale reads as
neutral. Discrete subsets take both ends, then the center, then fill each arm
evenly.

```{r, fig.height = 4}
show_portinari(category = "diverging")
```

`terra_roxa` sets the plum of a Portinari suit against the green of a coffee
plantation, a classic purple-green diverging scheme. It is colorblind-safe
for all nine colors, which makes it a good default for correlation matrices.

```{r, fig.height = 5, fig.width = 6}
cors <- cor(mtcars)
cors_long <- data.frame(
  x = factor(rep(colnames(cors), each = ncol(cors)), levels = colnames(cors)),
  y = factor(rep(colnames(cors), times = ncol(cors)), levels = rev(colnames(cors))),
  r = as.vector(cors)
)
ggplot(cors_long, aes(x, y, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", r)), size = 2.8,
            colour = ifelse(cors_long$r < -0.3 | cors_long$r > 0.55, "white", "grey15")) +
  scale_fill_portinari("terra_roxa", type = "continuous", limits = c(-1, 1),
                       name = "Correlation") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

```{r}
cars <- transform(mtcars, car = rownames(mtcars), diff = mpg - mean(mpg))
ggplot(cars, aes(diff, reorder(car, diff), fill = diff)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_portinari("guerra", type = "continuous", limits = c(-15, 15)) +
  labs(x = "mpg relative to the mean", y = NULL)
```

```{r}
likert <- data.frame(
  question = rep(paste("Question", 1:4), each = 5),
  answer = factor(rep(c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly agree"), 4),
                  levels = c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly agree")),
  share = c(10, 20, 30, 25, 15, 5, 15, 20, 35, 25, 20, 25, 25, 20, 10, 8, 12, 30, 30, 20)
)
ggplot(likert, aes(share, question, fill = answer)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_portinari("retirantes", name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "%", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Colorblind safety

`colorblind = TRUE` restricts any palette to colors that stay distinct under
protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia simulation.

```{r}
portinari.pal("sofia", colorblind = TRUE)
portinari.cvd.check("sofia")
```
